title: How effective is the R21/Matrix-M malaria vaccine in clinical trials?

answer:
The R21/Matrix-M malaria vaccine has shown high efficacy in clinical trials, although reported figures vary by trial phase and setting. It was well tolerated and offered high efficacy against clinical malaria in African children [1]. In Phase 2 trials, it demonstrated remarkable effectiveness reaching 77% [5]. Phase 3 trials reported 12-month vaccine efficacy of 75% at seasonal-transmission sites and 68% at standard sites, with efficacy against multiple clinical malaria episodes at 75% and 67%, respectively [5]. Other reports describe up to 77% protection against the malaria parasite [5].

Efficacy has not been uniform: results have varied across clinical trials conducted in different populations and settings [4]. A booster dose given one year after the primary three-dose regimen maintained high efficacy against first and multiple episodes of clinical malaria, and antibody concentrations correlated with vaccine efficacy [3]. Overall, the vaccine is considered among the most promising candidates, designed to be low-dose, cost-effective, and accessible [5].
